nodes.author: NGrandvaux
nodes.text:
A short thread about the viral outbreak reported in China.
1️⃣ The outbreak is caused by the human metapneumovirus (HMPV), which is NOT a new virus.
👉 It was identified in 2001 (though it had likely been circulating long before).
🔗 Reference: https://t.co/bi1GNDEl2A

nodes.author: NGrandvaux
nodes.text:
2️⃣ In Quebec, it was first described as early as 2002.
🔗 Reference: https://t.co/QHuMJZw6uE

nodes.author: NGrandvaux
nodes.text:
3️⃣ HMPV is monitored as part of respiratory virus surveillance in Quebec and Canada.
📊 You can find data for Quebec here:
🔗 https://t.co/6IUWA0VN5y 
(Take a look at the different pages, as analyses are categorized by settings: clinics/hospitals).

nodes.author: NGrandvaux
nodes.text:
4️⃣ For data across Canada:
🔗 Health Canada - Respiratory Virus Detections.
https://t.co/v4kTbKBina https://t.co/L8tXYA8u9y

nodes.author: NGrandvaux
nodes.text:
5️⃣ While HMPV is not harmless, there is no reason to compare this outbreak in China to the emergence of SARS-CoV-2.
⚠️ That said, it raises an important question:
Should we take measures to limit the spread of respiratory viruses?

nodes.author: NGrandvaux
nodes.text:
✅ Yes. These viruses have circulated before, of course, but we can improve human health by addressing them seriously.
🩺 Like other diseases that pose risks to human health, they deserve more attention.
🎯 Here, we have a clear opportunity for #prevention . So, let’s act on it!
